conviction_note: Near-null hunt: the event is a confirmed Q3 trading update (07:00-type bmo release); peer read-throughs (Whitbread, IHG) point to UK trading in line with what PPHE already said in August, Croatian national volumes were flat, and nothing found moves the FY26 bar (company-compiled EBITDA £140-147m), so the findings sum to about +0.05 while the scaled number (p_up 47 x abs 5.0 = -0.3) leans slightly negative only because this name has fallen on 5 of its last 7 results/trading-update days, including 'in line' ones; the two numbers differ in sign because the lean comes from the reaction function, not from any fact about Q3.

Q4 current trading / forward bookings commentary for the UK's important Q4; unknown.
Possible capital-allocation news on the ~$26.75m net New York proceeds (e.g. buyback or debt paydown); unknown, not signalled.
Arena Hospitality Group Q3 interim report likely published the same morning (2025 precedent: both 30 Oct 07:00); unknown.

bar: FY26 company-compiled analyst consensus: revenue £475.0-483.0m, EBITDA £140.0-147.0m as at 26 August 2026 (footnote 1 of the interim results, https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/pphe-hotel-group-ltd--pph/interim-results/9742113). findings.finding: UK peer read-through for Q3 is positive-to-in-line: Whitbread reported London ARR +2.7% and occupancy +1.2pp for the 26 weeks to 27 Aug 2026 'supported by a healthy events calendar', and UK&I RevPAR +3.2% in the first five weeks of H2 (Sept-early Oct); IHG's Q3 2026 update put UK RevPAR at +2.8% -- so PPHE's UK estate (~61% of H1 revenue) most likely grew through a tough Oasis-concert Q3 2025 comparative, consistent with its August 'continue to perform strongly'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 trading update with UK 'solid performance' and FY reiterated: +0.28%; Q1 2026 update with London-led +8% revenue: -7.86%; H1 2026 with UK RevPAR +5.2%: -6.95%. Good UK numbers have not been rewarded on print days.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the company itself told the market in August that UK trading continued strongly, so the read-through mostly confirms what is already in the price; what is not visibly priced is any upside from London holding growth through the September 2025 concert comparative (CoStar had London Sept 2025 RevPAR +8.9%). If the market had priced a beat, the stock would not sit 31% below the £22 'fair value' proposal and near its 60-day lows (run-up 60d -1.17%).
findings.independence: IHG Q3 2026 trading update, UK RevPAR +2.8% (https://www.ihgplc.com/en/news-and-media/news-releases/2026/third-quarter-trading-update-to-30-september-2026), a different company and dataset; comparative from CoStar Sept 2025 (https://www.costar.com/products/str-benchmark/resources/press-releases/september-concerts-boosted-london-hotel-performance).

findings.finding: Croatian national tourism volumes were flat through the peak season -- eVisitor Jan-Aug 2026 overnights +1%, August overnights +0.5%, Adriatic overnights +0.5%, with the minister citing shorter trips and careful travel budgets -- which gives no support to PPHE's August expectation that the 'gradual improvement in momentum' in Croatia (Arena, whose year is concentrated in Q3) would continue through the summer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: Croatia 'performed well during the peak months, with good rate growth more than offsetting a slight reduction in occupancy' despite poor August weather; the stock moved +0.28% that day.
findings.why_not_priced: A national volume series is a broad proxy that UK-listed holders of PPH rarely track; Arena's own Q3 has not been published (ZSE ARNT announcements show only own-share purchases up to 28 Oct 2026). But flat volumes are not a miss: PPHE has historically offset occupancy with rate, so the transmission to Arena's revenue is a hypothesis, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: Istria tourist board Jan-Sep 2026 statistics PDF (https://istra.hr/downloadf/istra_2026_01-09.pdf) could not be text-extracted here (snippet only: arrivals index ~103, nights ~101); none from a different source confirmed in document.

findings.finding: Arena Hospitality Group, PPHE's Zagreb-listed controlled subsidiary, has been buying back its own shares through the quarter and into the print window (ZSE own-share purchase notices on 7, 12, 15, 19, 23 and 28 October 2026, plus August-September).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction on PPH to Arena buyback notices.
findings.why_not_priced: Zagreb filings are not read by the PPH register; but a subsidiary buyback during its closed-ish period is at most a weak confidence signal and the money is small relative to PPHE, so it is close to worth nothing.

baseline_tension: Mild agreement: the baseline lean (+0.47, mostly short covering) and the flat 20-day run-up (+1.34%) sit beside a near-zero findings sum; the only directional pull is this name's own habit of falling on print days, which cuts slightly against the positive lean.
language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry -- the domestic RNS record (Investegate) supplied the event confirmation, the release-time precedent and the company-compiled consensus range, but those are the same documents any English-language reader sees; the only off-wire source was the Zagreb exchange (Arena) and the Croatian tourism series, which are Croatian-domestic rather than UK-domestic
lessons_applied: 'Size the move on what is new; let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': the Q3 numbers are not pre-released, so abs_move_pct went from 4.5 to 5.0 (between the 2.3% reiterated-guide and 7.4% new-numbers medians, thin $0.49m/day turnover); the habit of selling prints stays in p_up at 47 only

'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0' / inside-guidance rule: the UK peer read-through mostly confirms the company's own August statement, so it went from +0.4 to +0.25
'A narrow proxy loses ... macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': the Croatian national-volume finding went from -0.4 to -0.3
